summary: Controller RAM depends on `forks`: plan 1 GB per 10 forks plus a 2 GB reservation, so `forks=400` needs about 42 GB. When forks are fewer than hosts, more passes are needed; avoid RAM limits with rolling updates, provisioning callbacks, or when building images such as AMIs.
questions: How much memory does automation controller need per fork?
How do I size controller memory for forks?
What is a provisioning callback used for?

answer_card.title: Controller memory for forks
answer_card.answer_md:
RAM ≈ forks / 10 GB + 2 GB reserved.

| forks | RAM |
|---|---|
| 100 | 12 GB |
| 400 | 42 GB |

Fewer forks than hosts just means more passes. Rolling updates and provisioning callbacks reduce the need.
